parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Hydrogen chloride gas is made in the laboratory by adding concentrated sulfuric acid to potassium chloride.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Construct an equation for this reaction.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why hydrogen iodide is **not** prepared by adding concentrated sulfuric acid to sodium iodide.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
A sample of $\text{HI}\text{(g)}$ is added to a $2.00\text{ dm}^3$ sealed vessel at $764\text{ K}$ and allowed to reach equilibrium.

$$\text{reaction 1} \quad 2\text{HI}\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{I}_2\text{(g)} \quad K_{\text{c}} = 0.0217 \text{ at } 764\text{ K}$$

At equilibrium the mixture contains $1.70\text{ mol}$ of $\text{HI}\text{(g)}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: State **one** difference in the appearance of the initial reaction mixture compared to the mixture at equilibrium.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Deduce the expression for equilibrium constant $K_{\text{c}}$ for reaction 1.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the concentration of $\text{I}_2$ present in the reaction mixture at equilibrium. Show your working.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: The experiment is repeated at $500\text{ K}$. The value of $K_{\text{c}}$ under these conditions is $0.00625$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Describe the difference in the composition of the equilibrium mixture at $500\text{ K}$ compared to $764\text{ K}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Use Le Chatelier's principle to deduce whether the decomposition of $\text{HI}\text{(g)}$ is endothermic or exothermic. Explain your answer.
